title: Message Broker Selection
description: Learn to choose the right message broker for your microservices architecture.

data.text: Choosing the right message broker is critical for event-driven microservices. LinkedIn uses Kafka for 7 trillion messages per year, Netflix uses Kafka for event streaming, and many companies use RabbitMQ for reliable task queuing.

data.title: Broker Comparison
items: Apache Kafka: High-throughput, distributed event streaming platform
RabbitMQ: Mature message broker with flexible routing
AWS SQS/SNS: Managed queuing and pub/sub
Azure Service Bus: Enterprise messaging with transactions

data.text: Kafka is designed for high-throughput event streaming and log aggregation. It persists events durably and supports replay. RabbitMQ is designed for reliable message delivery with flexible routing patterns like topic exchanges. Choose Kafka for event streaming; choose RabbitMQ for task queuing and complex routing.

cards.title: RabbitMQ
cards.description: Mature message broker with flexible routing

data.title: Selection Criteria
data.text: Choose Kafka for event streaming, analytics pipelines, and log aggregation. Choose RabbitMQ for reliable task queuing, background jobs, and complex routing. Use managed services (SQS, Pub/Sub) when you do not want to operate infrastructure.

data.title: Example: Kafka Topic Design
data.code: Design Kafka topics with clear naming and partitioning strategy.

# Topic naming convention
# <domain>.<event-type>

order_events
  - Partition key: orderId
  - Retention: 7 days
  - Replication: 3

payment_events
  - Partition key: paymentId
  - Retention: 30 days
  - Replication: 3

user_events
  - Partition key: userId
  - Retention: 1 day
  - Replication: 3

# This ensures ordering within each entity

data.caption: Message broker decision flow

items.question: Can I use multiple brokers?
items.answer: Yes. Many companies use Kafka for event streaming and RabbitMQ for task queuing. Use the right tool for each use case.

items.question: What about Redis Streams?
items.answer: Redis Streams is suitable for lightweight event streaming when you already use Redis. It is simpler than Kafka but lacks durability and scalability for large-scale use.

items.question: Should I use managed brokers?
items.answer: Yes, if possible. Managed services like Confluent Cloud, AWS MSK, and CloudAMQP reduce operational overhead significantly.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Kafka excels at high-throughput event streaming
RabbitMQ is great for reliable task queuing
Choose based on throughput, routing, and operational needs
data.takeaway: Match the broker to your use case; do not default to one tool for everything.
